ranked.headline: Separating spatial context from cell identity in spatial transcriptomic variation
ranked.summary: New spatial methods partition expression into niche, abundance and intratype-state components and test differential expression with spatial localization.

ranked.headline: Frozen single-cell foundation models extended to multimodal completion and reconstruction
ranked.summary: scAnyOmics, MUTUAL and Top2All reuse frozen or pretrained single-cell models for cross-modality tasks, while BioTrajX adds trajectory plausibility metrics.

ranked.headline: Evaluation protocol, not architecture, drives molecular property prediction benchmarks
ranked.summary: Protocol-matched and scaffold-split ADMET benchmarks now test whether acquisition, tuning and encoder choice actually improve prediction.

ranked.headline: Inferring unmeasured spatial omics layers from histology, transcripts and host signals
ranked.summary: New preprints predict proteins, pathogens and transcriptomes from other spatial modalities, and one benchmarks cross-slice protein imputation directly.

ranked.headline: Packaged software integrates capture probe and oligo pool library design workflows
ranked.summary: BaitBench and PoolParty package hybrid capture probe and oligo pool design as single tools, alongside other packaged analysis pipelines and databases.

ranked.headline: Sequence-to-function models predict regulatory consequences of noncoding variants
ranked.summary: Fine-tuning on MPRA labels and added 3D chromatin context are newly extending sequence-based variant effect models.

ranked.headline: Agents and foundation models tested against baselines across omics analysis tasks
ranked.summary: Recent LLM agent and benchmark papers report explicit accuracy, transferability, and failure-mode measures for omics analysis tasks.

ranked.headline: Curated microbial catalogs and long-read profiling feed functional inference in microbiomes
ranked.summary: Recent releases of PLATE, CAnDi, and BacMap 3.0 organize microbial genomic data by environment, host, and taxonomy for downstream inference.

ranked.headline: Learned models resolve cell-context effects in neurodegeneration and brain datasets
ranked.summary: Interpretable models now couple spatially and cell-type-resolved readouts to genetic and mechanistic validation in neurodegeneration research.

ranked.headline: Isoform quantification methods target mapping ambiguity and bias in RNA-seq
ranked.summary: Recent preprints add context-aware MAPQ filtering, transcript-specific k-mers, and alignment-free self-benchmarking to isoform quantification.

ranked.headline: Transcriptomic models are evaluated by transfer design, calibration and identifiability
ranked.summary: Six preprints test whether transcriptomic inferences hold across cohorts, source contexts, cell states and statistical nulls, not just in-sample fit.

ranked.headline: Consolidated platforms standardize access to spatial and single-cell transcriptomics data
ranked.summary: Expanding spatial and single-cell resources now span tissue atlases, subcellular transcript databases, and reproducible analysis workflows.

ranked.headline: Imaging and spatial data tools embed attribution, heterogeneity modeling and benchmarking
ranked.summary: Nine new tools convert microscopy, histology and spatial transcriptomics into quantitative readouts, with benchmarks and attribution built in.

ranked.headline: Predicting single-cell responses to perturbations with regulatory constraints
ranked.summary: Perturbation-response models are now being coupled to cross-context transfer and explicit regulatory, pathway or dynamical constraints.

ranked.headline: Pretrained sequence models are reused for variant, structure, and site prediction
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and one published study extend pretrained DNA, RNA, and protein sequence models to variant and site prediction.

ranked.headline: Cell-type-resolved omics resources harmonize heterogeneous data for queryable access
ranked.summary: Recent resources integrate cell-type-resolved methylation, eQTL and single-cell data with disease outcomes and drug response in queryable form.

ranked.headline: Network visualization tools add 3D layers, omics coupling, and group-aware layouts
ranked.summary: Three recent preprints extend interactive tooling for multilayered and annotated biological networks, from 3D web exploration to R containers.

ranked.headline: Reference choice shapes variant and regulatory analysis in plant and human genomes
ranked.summary: Composite and pangenome references are being benchmarked against conventional assemblies for somatic, regulatory, and mitochondrial variant analysis.

ranked.headline: Scaffolding and evaluation determine reliability of biomedical LLM agents
ranked.summary: Preprints now test whether scaffolding, not model tier, governs LLM agent reliability in biological hypothesis generation, bioinformatics and evaluation tasks.

ranked.headline: Deep sequence models decode transcription initiation and enhancer activity from DNA
ranked.summary: Interpretable sequence models now map initiation, promoter motifs and enhancers, while sex-biased enhancer activity is quantified across human tissues.

ranked.headline: Whole-genome doubling tracked as subclonal evolution across human cancers
ranked.summary: Pan-cancer and single-cell work now resolve WGD as clonal fraction rather than a binary tumour classification.

ranked.headline: Auditable predictions for protein yield, structure search, and proteome recoding
ranked.summary: Predictive and LLM-based protein analyses are now reported with explicit calibration, verification, or provenance rather than as unchecked outputs.

ranked.headline: Inferring microbial taxonomy directly from long-read and metagenomic sequencing data
ranked.summary: Long-read amplicons and pretrained genomic language models are being benchmarked for species-level microbial taxonomy from raw reads.

ranked.headline: Tools linking structure prediction, bioactivity data and genomes to peptide candidates
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and the DBAASP V4 release pair structure prediction and curated bioactivity data with candidate-level outputs for discovery.

ranked.headline: Curated resources link experimental binding and specificity data to molecular structures
ranked.summary: Recent releases add experimental affinities, ML-ready splits, and AlphaFold 3 TCR specificity predictions across viral, cancer, and autoimmune epitopes.

ranked.headline: Chromosome-scale genomes reveal organelle-host metabolism and sex chromosome evolution
ranked.summary: Recent assemblies across haptophytes and mosses link resolved genome structure to organelle metabolism and recombination history.

ranked.headline: Learned and accelerated methods now operate directly on raw reads and pileups
ranked.summary: Raw-read and pileup inputs now feed deep learning models, while throughput and memory behavior are measured explicitly at scale.

ranked.headline: Deep learning models decode 3D chromatin architecture from Hi-C contact matrices
ranked.summary: Matrix-native neural architectures now address subcompartment annotation, TAD boundary calling, and Hi-C resolution enhancement directly from contact maps.

ranked.headline: Computational tools standardize benchmarking and interpretation of variants
ranked.summary: Recent resources extend variant interpretation from coding missense scoring to mtDNA non-coding, structural, and copy-number variants.

ranked.headline: Generative models produce protein conformational ensembles guided by experimental data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple sequence-, cryo-EM-, and DEER-conditioned generative models to produce conformational ensembles rather than single structures.

ranked.headline: Coupled Models Link Chromatin Organization to Hydration and Cohesin Kinetics
ranked.summary: Coupled mechanistic models now infer kinetic and encounter parameters from structural signatures, not just predict organization.

ranked.headline: Refining covariate adjustment and replicability assessment in GWAS and metabolomics
ranked.summary: Covariate-adjusted binary and medication-adjusted GWAS now have dedicated bias-correction methods, alongside new UK Biobank metabolomics resources.

ranked.headline: Molecular profiles are being linked to individual clinical outcome predictions
ranked.summary: Pre-treatment single-cell and methylation profiles now enable individual-level predictions of toxicity, survival, and immune trajectories.

ranked.headline: Modeling glioblastoma invasion and proliferation from MRI and single-cell imaging data
ranked.summary: Single-timepoint MRI and ex vivo single-cell imaging now allow mechanistic parameters of glioblastoma invasion to be estimated through explicit models.

ranked.headline: Graph pangenomes and simulation reveal structural variation driving genome evolution
ranked.summary: Graph pangenomes and forward simulation now resolve structural variants and transposable element dynamics across isolate genomes.

ranked.headline: New tools predict RNA structure, binding sites and validate models from sequence
ranked.summary: Deep-learning structure predictors are being benchmarked on RNA and protein-RNA complexes, exposing accuracy limits on novel RNA folds.

ranked.headline: Explicit reference criteria for evaluating biological model outputs and representations
ranked.summary: Three recent preprints test biological models against explicit references in genome folding, cryo-EM map comparison, and EEG seizure detection.

ranked.headline: Mechanical and diffusive forces modelled as generators of tissue and pattern geometry
ranked.summary: Recent preprints model how mechanical and diffusive forces generate tissue and pattern geometry, with connectivity changing during growth.

ranked.headline: Structural modelling links disease-associated variants to altered protein features
ranked.summary: Structure-based modelling and MD simulations now map disease-linked missense variants onto protein interfaces, hydration sites and interaction networks.

ranked.headline: Learned priors and fragment-ion evidence under validation in MS/MS identification
ranked.summary: Benchmarks show shared de novo peptide errors from limited fragment coverage, alongside new fragment-ion and structural priors for MS/MS identification.
